:::{#exm-surprisal-log-half}
#### Halvings of certainty for a loaded coin
<!-- no-figure: the example reports a handful of numbers, with nothing to plot -->

A coin lands heads with [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $0.2$. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
The chunk computes the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) of heads in two ways:
as $-\log_2 0.2$,
and as the base one half logarithm of $0.2$.

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
p_heads <- 0.2
from_base_two <- -log(x = p_heads, base = 2)
from_base_half <- log(x = p_heads, base = 0.5)
c(from_base_two, from_base_half)
```

Both give $`r round(from_base_half, 3)`$ bits (@thm-surprisal-log-half).
Halving $1$ that many times gives $0.5^{`r round(from_base_half, 3)`} = `r round(0.5^from_base_half, 3)`$, the probability of heads.

:::
